class.name: RecommendedGraphics
class.brief_description: Graphics settings recommended for the computer the game runs on.
class.description:
Recommends graphics settings in tiers, from [constant TIER_ULTRA] down to [constant TIER_LOW]. [method get_tier] picks a starting tier from the graphics adapter, [method get_settings] gives a tier's engine settings for the screen or a headset and [method apply] sets them on a viewport. [method benchmark] measures the tiers in the game itself and keeps the best one that holds a frame rate. The player's tier is the option [code]display/graphics_tier[/code] in [Options], which starts as [method get_tier] recommends and is applied as the game starts and whenever it changes. A game adds its own settings to each tier (draw distance, crowd density) as the option changes: [codeblock] const TIERS := ["ultra", "high", "medium", "low"]
func _ready() -> void: _apply_tier(Options.get_value("display/graphics_tier")) Options.changed.connect(func(key, value): if key == "display/graphics_tier": _apply_tier(value))
func _apply_tier(tier: String) -> void: crowd_density = [1.0, 1.0, 0.6, 0.3][TIERS.find(tier)]
func _on_use_recommended_pressed() -> void: await RecommendedGraphics.benchmark(func(tier): Options.set_value("display/graphics_tier", TIERS[tier]), 60.0) [/codeblock] With [code]rendering/graphics_tier/apply[/code] off in Project Settings, the game applies the engine's settings itself with [method get_settings] and [method apply].

method.name: apply
method.description: Sets [param settings] (from [method get_settings]) on [param viewport]. Each key is the name of a [Viewport] property, except [code]directional_shadow_size[/code], which sets the size of the directional shadow atlas (see [method RenderingServer.directional_shadow_atlas_set_size]).

method.name: benchmark
method.description: Measures the tiers in the game as it is running, best first. For each tier, calls [param apply_tier] with the tier, waits for it to settle and times every frame for a few seconds. It stops at the first tier that draws nine frames in ten within [param target_fps] (to within 5%), or at [constant TIER_LOW]. Await the returned signal for the tier chosen, which is applied when it completes. Vertical sync and [member Engine.max_fps] are lifted while it measures (each frame, so a game applying a tier through its own settings doesn't put them back), so a display's refresh rate doesn't hide how fast a tier can go, and put back after. In a headset they stay: the headset paces the frames, and its refresh rate is the target to give. Runs while the game is paused, so it can run from a settings menu. Only one benchmark runs at a time.

method.name: get_settings
method.description: Returns the engine settings recommended for [param tier] on the screen, or in a headset when [param headset] is [code]true[/code]. The keys are [code]scaling_3d_mode[/code], [code]scaling_3d_scale[/code], [code]msaa_3d[/code], [code]screen_space_aa[/code], [code]use_taa[/code], [code]anisotropic_filtering_level[/code], [code]mesh_lod_threshold[/code], [code]directional_shadow_size[/code], [code]contact_shadows[/code] (screen-space contact shadows, [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/contact_shadow/enabled]: on in [constant TIER_ULTRA] and [constant TIER_HIGH], never in a headset) and [code]skip_mipmaps[/code] ([member ProjectSettings.rendering/textures/quality/skip_mipmaps]: [constant TIER_LOW] loads 3D textures without their largest level, a quarter of the memory, for textures loaded from then on). Apply them with [method apply]. Each tier below [constant TIER_ULTRA] draws at most so many pixels, so it upscales further on larger screens; [constant TIER_HIGH] draws a 4K screen at full size and a 5K one at about 85%, [constant TIER_LOW] draws 1080p at 70% and 4K at about half. In a headset, the lower tiers limit the pixels drawn for each eye the same way. Where a tier upscales, it uses a temporal upscaler when it smooths with TAA and a spatial one otherwise: MetalFX where the device supports it, FSR elsewhere. With the Mobile renderer, which has no TAA or temporal upscaling, FXAA takes TAA's place. A headset never uses TAA (it smears as the head turns), so it smooths with MSAA.

method.name: get_tier
method.description: Returns the tier the graphics adapter suggests. It reads the generation and class from the adapter's name (an RTX 4070's generation 40 and class 70, an M4 Max's generation 4 and Max), so later generations get a sensible tier too. Laptop graphics sit a step lower than the desktop card of the same name. Adapters from families it doesn't recognize go by their type: discrete ones [constant TIER_MEDIUM], others [constant TIER_LOW]. It's a first guess for a first run; [method benchmark] measures it.

constants.constant: The best: everything at full size and quality.
High settings, drawing a 4K screen at full size.
Medium settings, for discrete graphics a few generations old.
